body.technical_summary: Apply H-1: the auth interceptor reads from an in-memory store that is empty during the rehydration tick after refresh. Await rehydration before issuing the first request.
implementation_plan: step -> verify: add an explicit `await store.rehydrated` in the interceptor before reading the token; verify by re-running the probe harness.
step -> verify: add a regression test in firefox e2e suite; verify it fails on main and passes after the fix.
assumptions: The auth store exposes a `rehydrated` promise; if not, the fix may need to expose one.
design_notes: Keep the await inside the interceptor only; do not change app-level boot order.
rollback_plan: Revert the single commit; behavior returns to pre-fix state.

planned_changes.rationale: Await rehydration so the Authorization header is non-empty after refresh.
Pin the fix with a CI-runnable regression test.

execution_handoff.code_change_summary: Await store.rehydrated in the auth interceptor; add a Firefox regression test.
risk_areas: interceptor latency on first request; bounded by store rehydrate time (<10ms)

test_scenarios.statement: After refresh in Firefox, /api/me returns 200 with valid token.

test_commands.purpose: Run the regression test in headless Firefox.
